chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about buying meat from the market, without knowing what the butchers do with it. He said, 'If it is in the market of the Muslims, eat it and do not ask about it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat from the market if you don't know how it was slaughtered?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* articulates the principle of *istishab al-hal* (presumption of continuity of the original state) regarding meat from the general Muslim market (*sūq al-muslimīn*), where the default assumption is permissibility unless proven otherwise. It reflects the Shia juristic consensus that uncertainty (*shakk*) does not negate the initial halal status, thereby relieving the consumer from the burden of verifying every specific slaughter act, a ruling distinct from cases where the slaughterer is known to be non-Muslim or specific conditions of *dhikr* are in doubt.
